01.r: He takes his seat at the work, like a metalworker at the furnace.
01.n: A perfect with 'and', which carries the prophecy into the future: 'he shall sit'. YLT renders the perfect form literally, 'he hath sat'. Gesenius gives the first sense as TO SIT, TO SIT DOWN.

02.r: Melting the metal to separate it from its dross.
02.n: A participle, 'one refining', the same word as 'refiner' in the verse before. Gesenius: TO MELT a metal, specially to purge gold or silver by fire, and figuratively to prove, to examine; Geneva's 'to trye' takes that second sense.

03.r: Making the metal clean of what is mixed into it.
03.n: Gesenius gives the root sense TO SHINE, TO BE BRIGHT, then to be clean or pure, in a physical, a Levitical or a moral sense; this form means to make clean. A reasonable reading is that the metal picture and the priestly sense of 'clean' meet here.

04.n: Gesenius says silver is so called from its pale colour.

05.r: The refining now applied to people.
05.n: The same verb as 'purifying' earlier in the verse, now as a finite verb with 'and', future in sense.

06.r: Marks 'the sons of Levi' as the object of 'purify'.
06.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'the sons of'.

07.r: The descendants of Levi: the priestly tribe.

08.r: The ancestor of the priestly tribe, standing for the tribe itself.
08.n: Gesenius notes that the tribe of Levi, the 'sons of Levi', was set apart for the service of the sanctuary, and that the priesthood belonged to the family of Aaron within it.

09.r: Clear them of impurity as metal is cleared.
09.n: A different verb from 'refining' earlier in the verse. Gesenius gives its sense as TO SQUEEZE THROUGH a strainer, to strain, hence to refine wine and metals. 'Purge' keeps the two verbs apart in our English.

12.n: The 'like' is repeated in the Hebrew: 'like the gold and like the silver'. The DRC and YLT keep it.

13.r: Describes what the purified priests will go on doing.
13.n: Literally 'and they shall be to the LORD bringers near of an offering'. 'Be' with a participle describes ongoing action, so 'they shall be bringing near'; it can also be read 'they shall belong to the LORD, bringing near an offering'.

15.r: Bringing an offering to the altar.
15.n: The causative form of the verb 'to draw near': 'make come near'. The brief's lexicon gives this form as to cause to approach, bring near.

16.n: Gesenius lists a gift, tribute, and a gift offered to a divinity, specially a sacrifice without blood. Here it is a gift to God, not tribute to a ruler. The Hebrew is singular; most translations make it plural.

17.r: Offered as it ought to be, by priests now made right.
17.n: Gesenius gives the first sense as rectitude, right, before justice. 'In righteousness' can mean in the right way or in a right state; both fit here, and the choice is a matter of reading.

_extra.7: καὶ (and): begins a phrase added by the Greek translators, 'and as the gold'.
_extra.8: ὡς (as): part of the added phrase.
_extra.9: τὸ (the): part of the added phrase.
_extra.10: χρυσίον (gold): the Greek adds gold to the first mention of silver, 'as the silver and as the gold'.

01.n: καθιεῖται, 'he will sit', a future of καθίζω. The Greek has no 'and' here.

04.n: The Greek makes the silver a comparison: 'refining and cleansing as the silver'.

09.n: χέω, 'to pour': the Greek reads 'and he will pour them', as molten metal is poured.

11.n: The first word is printed σπερ in our Greek text; it is evidently ὥσπερ, 'just as', cut short.

16.n: θυσία, 'sacrifice', where the Hebrew has a word whose first sense is a gift. The DRC's 'sacrifices' matches this.
